messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High tail latency detected on prod inference fleet (shard-prod-12). p99 > 6s, sustained for 4m. Alerts triggered: SLO-breach, streaming-stalls. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/prod/kv_cache

sarah_oncall: saw it — I’m on it. pinging runtime & sre.

raj_runtime: joining. initial read: eviction-rate spiked on shard-prod-12, prefill queue depth high, decode-worker backlog growing.

maria_sre: confirming from traces: a subset of streaming sessions are experiencing chunked responses — streams stall at tail. p95 up from 120ms -> 1.8s, p99 6.2s.

kevin_custsuccess: getting customer pings. Two large customers reported timeouts for streaming transcriptions ~2-5m ago. Not widespread yet but high-visibility.

raj_runtime: logs show a big jump in KV cache eviction churn:
```
# aggregated from metrics api
kv.evictions_total{shard="prod-12"} 3124
kv.prefill.requests_in_flight 842
decode.worker.queue_length 410
```
This smells like fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance. prefill storms are filling KV with long prefixes that are then evicted before decode finishes.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0358. Pager duty: paged oncall-sre. playbook link: https://playbooks.internal/kv-cache-frag

tess_infra: quick mitigation options: 1) raise eviction threshold for prod-12 (reduces churn), 2) temporarily disable aggressive prefill for affected model-family, 3) route new streams to fallback warm pool.

sarah_oncall: prioritize minimal blast radius: start with 2 and 3 in parallel. raj, can you flip prefill toggle for model set id mset-42? tess, can you add routing rule to steer new sessions off prod-12 -> prod-06 warm pool?

raj_runtime: working on toggle. API call:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" \
  https://controlplane.internal/configs/prefill/toggle \
  -d '{"model_set":"mset-42","enabled":false}' | jq .
```
Applying now.

maria_sre: I’m putting a throttling policy on prefill producer for prod-12 until we have stable p99.

(2m later)

raj_runtime: prefill disabled for mset-42 on prod-12. Confirmed requests_in_flight dropping from 842 -> 120. decode queue length trending down.

ops-bot: Change: routing-rule added -> new streams for customer tier default now prefer prod-06 (warm pool) for 30m.

kevin_custsuccess: customers that reported problems say they see fewer timeouts. Asking for rough ETA.

maria_sre: p95 down to 420ms, p99 down to 2.1s — improving but still above SLO for some streaming tails. Evictions reduced by ~70%.

raj_runtime: also saw fragmentation in KV segments: small dense segments causing inefficient memory layout. We can trigger a background compaction but that’s a heavier op. Options: light compaction to clean hot prefixes + increase per-shard cache size for prod-12 (short term).

tess_infra: I can bump cache allocation for prod-12 by 10% for 15m to buy time. Doing that now.

(1m later)

ops-bot: config change applied: prod-12 cache +10% for 15m (rollback in 15m).

maria_sre: p95 = 210ms, p99 = 920ms. Streaming stalls largely resolved; tail still occasionally spikes when large prefills hit.

kevin_custsuccess: relaying to customers: "We implemented routing and mitigations; monitoring shows latency improving. We'll follow up with root cause & timeline." They asked for ETA for permanent fix.

raj_runtime: root cause hypothesis so far: simultaneous traffic pattern shift (long-context streaming sessions) + aggressive prefill policy introduced last week for mset-42. TTL/eviction policy combined with fragmented KV allocation caused churn: hot entries evicted too early, causing repeated cold decodes and refills -> tail cost.

sarah_oncall: notes for post-incident: capture prefill throttle metrics, eviction histograms, allocation fragmentation snapshots, and list customers impacted. Also capture the recent config change that deployed last week (mset-42 aggressive prefill).

maria_sre: action items (short):
- keep prefill disabled for mset-42 for now
- keep routing rule for 30m and monitor
- schedule light compaction during low traffic window (SLA permitting)
- plan controlled rollback of aggressive prefill config from last week in next deploy window

raj_runtime: long term: add backpressure on prefill while decode backlog > X, smarter prefill prioritization by decode progress, and compaction autotune. Also add alert that correlates prefill_in_flight and decode_queue so we catch imbalance earlier.

ops-bot: Runbook update suggested: add explicit "prefill vs decode imbalance" checklist and add runbook step to route streaming -> warm pools. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runbooks/pull/129

sarah_oncall: handing off to next oncall (maria) in 30m with summary. If anyone escalates, ping me and I’ll rejoin.

maria_sre: I’m taking the handoff — will monitor for 2h and coordinate postmortem draft. Leaving prefill disabled and cache bump active.

kevin_custsuccess: will follow up with customers with the summary and timeframe for permanent fix.

sarah_oncall: TL;DR: KV cache fragmentation + aggressive prefill caused eviction churn -> decode backlog -> streaming tail stalls. Mitigations applied: prefill disabled for offending model set, routing off hot shard to warm pool, small cache bump, scheduled compaction + runbook updates.

maria_sre: adding retrospective note: we should add canary gating for prefill changes and an automated circuit-breaker when evictions_rate > threshold.

(incident status: mitigated, postmortem pending)
